title: Live command timing and decision-effort instrumentation
description: Objective: make the production daemon/control-room path emit the benchmark's distinct timing and human-effort source observations instead of asking the harness to accept caller-supplied timestamp pairs. Deliverable: daemon command/event and control-room live instrumentation that binds trigger, server receipt/commit, client receipt, render and human commit observations to one command/run identity; records demanded decision commands, free interactions, focus/away intervals, attention switches and recovery burden; then feeds the existing SurfaceTimingReceipt evaluator through a real consumer edge. MEASURED GAP at HEAD 2b15b8f: daemon StreamEvent exposes only committedAt; live-event-feed copies only wire fields; evaluateTiming exists but has zero production call sites and accepts caller-supplied pairs; wire events omit commandId/actor/session needed for effort attribution, and no focus/activity or decision-effort record exists. Consumer: task-b937811e8b72459ea169e5fff1238ce1. NOT in scope: benchmark statistics, thresholds, competitor screen-capture instrumentation, corpus/campaign, UI claim verdicts, or provider usage. Owned paths: focused daemon HTTP/stream telemetry fields, generated client/live control-room instrumentation, and tests; preserve existing truth boundaries. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test && pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: The live production path binds trigger, server-received/committed, client-received, surface-rendered and human-command-committed observations to exact project/session/command/event/run identities; no layer compares timestamps from different clocks without an explicit observer/clock binding.

System latency and response time remain separate, away/focus intervals are recorded separately, and absent/unparseable/skewed observations return the existing or new stable UNKNOWN code plus exact layer instead of zero/absolute-value interpolation.

Demanded decision commands, free interactions, attention switches, recovery actions/burden and scroll/focus evidence are emitted as frozen observations with explicit source/provenance; the live path can distinguish create/approve/accept from any additional demanded decision.

At least one actual live control-room surface calls evaluateTiming/describeTimingReceipt using observed production timestamps, and daemon/client/control-room tests prove the real edge rather than a fixture-only helper.
Refusal tests pin exact code/layer and zero-vs-absent precedence; generated timing/decision cases assert non-zero exact cardinality, including every timing split and decision kind.

Mutation drills bypass a production render timestamp and a decision-command attribution guard and turn named live integration tests red; fresh pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test && pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test && pnpm typecheck exits 0.
taskRails: Do not collapse server, stream/client receipt, render and human time; response time is not system latency.
Do not compare cross-machine timestamps without an explicit shared observer or clock-offset uncertainty; unresolved skew is UNKNOWN.
Instrumentation is observational and grants no authority or evidence strength.
No benchmark thresholds, gate scoring, competitor screen-capture or confirmatory corpus bytes belong here.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; the cap is per file.

implementationPlan.description:

The description's gaps were confirmed at HEAD 2b15b8f/6ffb4fe and all three children have landed since, so every claim is STALE BY DEFAULT and must be re-run. This binds in BOTH directions: do not build something the description calls missing until a grep confirms it is missing. No production bytes written in this step.

Run and record:
1. `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
2. `grep -rn evaluateTiming --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx apps/ packages/ | grep -v '\.test\.'` — EXPECTED CLOSED: wire-timing.ts:212 calls it, command-latency.tsx:107 calls describeTimingReceipt. If zero non-test hits reappear, the edge regressed and the plan changes.
3. `sed -n '43,58p' apps/daemon/src/http/event-stream-contract.ts` — EXPECTED CLOSED: StreamEvent carries commandId and decisionTrace.
4. `grep -rln 'effort\|Effort' apps/control-room/src/live/` — EXPECTED STILL EMPTY. This is THE finding: the effort-records/admission/collector/intervals family has no live consumer. If it now returns files, a peer has wired it; STOP and re-plan rather than landing a second edge.
5. Verify the reachability chain the new edge will join: main.tsx:8 -> live-app.tsx:10 -> live-event-feed.ts:4-6 -> wire-timing.ts.
6. `grep -c ''` on live-dispatch.ts (expect ~271, already over the 250 target), live-app.tsx, live-event-feed.ts, effort-collector.ts.
7. READ `apps/control-room/src/live/live-timing-path.test.tsx` end to end, especially its header at :10-19. Its shape is the specification for the test you will write in step 2, and its stated reason is the reason.

TDD — WRITE THE FAILING LIVE INTEGRATION TEST FIRST. Create `apps/control-room/src/live/live-effort-path.test.tsx`, modelled on live-timing-path.test.tsx.

ITS SHAPE IS THE POINT, and getting it wrong makes the whole task vacuous. DO NOT import `createEffortCollector`, feed it a decision and assert the returned record — the effort-records/admission unit specs already do exactly that, and they have passed for the entire time production had ZERO callers. That is precisely why this gap stayed invisible. Instead:
- Render the live application (LiveControlRoom with its ClockProvider, as live-timing-path.test.tsx does).
- Drive a REAL demanded decision command through the live dispatch seam — one of the kinds live-dispatch.ts already handles: `planning.create_draft`, `plan.approve`, `integration.accept_output`.
- Assert the effort observation production computed: its decision kind, its source/provenance, and its layer. Every asserted value must be one production produced; nothing in the test may hand the surface a record, a decision kind, or a reason code.

Cover what DoD 3 names: the live path distinguishes create/approve/accept from an ADDITIONAL demanded decision. Assert the DECISION KIND that came back, not merely that some record exists.

Assert a refusal case with its EXACT code and layer — EFFORT_OBSERVATION_UNPARSEABLE and its EffortLayer — never merely that the operation did not succeed, and name which layer refused since more than one can.

This test MUST FAIL at this point: nothing under live/ imports effort today. A test that passes before step 3 lands is testing something other than the edge, and that is the defect to fix before continuing.

LAND THE MISSING LIVE CONSUMER EDGE. Create `apps/control-room/src/live/live-effort-edge.ts`, mirroring how live-event-feed.ts wired wire-timing.ts into the live poll path — this is the symmetric seam on the dispatch side, and mirroring it is deliberate rather than incidental.

The module owns the collector wiring and nothing else: create the collector via `createEffortCollector()`, observe a demanded decision command as the live path issues it, and record the free interactions, focus/away intervals, attention switches and recovery burden the existing vocabulary already names (INTERVAL_KINDS is ["AWAY","FOCUS"], RECOVERY_BURDENS and DECISION_KINDS are frozen in effort-records.ts).

SHAPING ONLY, NEVER INFERENCE — the discipline live-event-feed.ts states in its own header and this module must inherit: an identity the dispatch seam did not state stays null rather than becoming an empty string; nothing is derived by subtraction; an unobtainable observation records its stable UNKNOWN code from EFFORT_UNKNOWN_CODES rather than implying that nothing happened. Instrumentation is observational and grants no authority (task rail 3).

RE-DECLARE NOTHING. Every code, layer, decision kind and interval kind is imported from effort-records.ts. If you find yourself typing a string literal that already exists in that file's frozen arrays, you are duplicating the authority child task-bcae0b7e landed.

Do NOT create a physical `.js` bridge: apps/control-room does not use them (only .ts/.tsx/.css under live/), unlike apps/daemon and packages/**. Keep the file under 250 lines, measured with `grep -c ''`.

WIRE THE ONE DURABLE CALL SITE (Clause 1: 'exports the symbols' is not composition; a real call site is).

Add the import plus ONE call into `apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch.ts` at `dispatchAffordance` (:243), which is where the live path actually issues commands and already handles exactly the kinds DoD 3 names — `planning.create_draft` (:30), `plan.approve` (:104), `integration.accept_output` (:156,:161), `goal.create` (:94), `review.submit` (:196).

KEEP THE EDIT SMALL AND DELIBERATE. live-dispatch.ts is ALREADY 271 lines — over the 250 target and under the 400 split point. The observation logic belongs in live-effort-edge.ts; this file receives an import and a call, nothing more. Re-measure with `grep -c ''` after the edit and confirm it has not grown materially.

Do not change dispatch behaviour. The observation is a side record: a command that dispatched before this change must dispatch identically after it, and a failure to record an observation must never fail a dispatch. If recording can throw, contain it and record the stable UNKNOWN code instead — instrumentation may not acquire the power to break the thing it observes.

Run the step-2 test. It must now PASS. If it still fails, the edge is not reachable from the rendered path and the wiring is wrong — fix the wiring, never the assertion.

DRILL A — BYPASS A PRODUCTION RENDER TIMESTAMP (DoD 6, first drill). Capture `sha256sum` of the target BEFORE mutating.

Target: `apps/control-room/src/performance/wire-timing.ts`. The render phase is computed at :208 as `render: pairing(TIMING_PHASE_OBSERVERS.render, input.received, input.rendered)`, with `rendered` declared at :189 and readings taken through `readClientClock` at :149. Bypass the production render observation — for example make the render pairing use `input.received` at both ends, so the span production observed collapses to a number no clock produced.

NAMED TEST THAT MUST REDDEN: `apps/control-room/src/live/live-timing-path.test.tsx`. Its own header states the 30 ms gap 'is a span production observed between two moments, not a number this test handed it', so this drill is exactly what it was written to catch.

Confirm it reddens ON THE TIMING ASSERTION, not on a crash, an unhandled rejection, or a render error — a crash is not a refusal and proves the module was reached, not that the assertion is load-bearing.

Restore by Edit, then verify the restore by `sha256sum` against the captured hash. NEVER restore with `git checkout` (reverts to HEAD, destroying this task's uncommitted work) and never accept an empty `git diff` as proof (blind to untracked paths — the two new files in this task are untracked).

DRILL B — WEAKEN THE DECISION-COMMAND ATTRIBUTION GUARD (DoD 6, second drill). This is the drill that had NO valid target before this task: weakening the guard today reddens only a unit test in performance/, because no live integration test for effort existed. Steps 2-4 gave it one.

Capture `sha256sum` first. Target: `apps/control-room/src/performance/effort-admission.ts:127-136`, where `demandedKind` is read (:127), `ADDITIONAL_DECISION_KIND` is separated (:131), membership is gated by `asMember(demanded, BASELINE_DECISION_KINDS)` (:134) and the refusal `EFFORT_OBSERVATION_UNPARSEABLE` is raised (:135). Weaken it — for example accept any string as a demanded kind instead of requiring membership, or let an ADDITIONAL decision be attributed as a baseline kind.

NAMED TEST THAT MUST REDDEN: the new `apps/control-room/src/live/live-effort-path.test.tsx`, on the decision-kind or reason-code assertion.

A GREEN DRILL HERE IS A DEFECT IN THE TEST, NOT A PASS. If the live test stays green, the edge is not really carrying the attribution — the test is passing for some other reason. Fix the test or the wiring and re-run; do not record a green drill as satisfying DoD 6, and do not fall back to reddening the performance/ unit test, which is precisely the fixture-only proof this task exists to replace.

Also confirm WHICH LAYER answered. More than one layer can refuse here (EFFORT_ADMISSION_LAYER vs EFFORT_COLLECTOR_LAYER); a drill that reddens because a different layer started answering first has not proven the guard you targeted.

Restore by Edit and verify by `sha256sum`.

THE FOUR-PACKAGE GATE (DoD 6), each leg's exit code read SEPARATELY. The task's verification line chains them with `&&`, which stops at the first red and reports one status for four legs; a piped run reports the pipe's tail. Run four independent commands and record each verbatim:
1. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test; echo "DAEMON_EXIT=$?"`
2. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test; echo "CLIENT_EXIT=$?"`
3. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test; echo "CONTROL_ROOM_EXIT=$?"`
4. `pnpm typecheck; echo "TYPECHECK_EXIT=$?"`

Also confirm the pre-existing suites this change sits next to still pass unchanged: live-timing-path.test.tsx, live-command-timing.test.tsx, live-event-feed.test.ts, and the effort-* specs in performance/.

WATCH FOR WHOLE-PAYLOAD EQUALITY. If a live payload assertion elsewhere reddens, check whether the new observation entered a structure some test compares wholesale rather than field by field — that failure belongs to this diff and must be fixed here, not disclosed as foreign.

LINE BUDGET: `grep -c ''` on live-effort-edge.ts (under 250) and live-dispatch.ts (must not have grown materially from its pre-existing 271).

FOREIGN RED: `pnpm typecheck` is repo-wide and this worktree is shared — a peer's in-flight drill has already flipped a file mid-session today. Apply the path-attributed-baseline rail: record repo-wide failures at the merge-base, at HEAD, subtract, and intersect with this task's owned paths (apps/control-room/src/live/**). That intersection must be EMPTY. Disclose any foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines and paths; never repair it, never hide it, never fabricate green.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, COMMIT, HANDOFF. Invoke the adversarial-self-review skill, then work the checklist aimed at how THIS task fails while looking finished:

1. Is the new live test actually a LIVE test? If it imports `createEffortCollector` directly and asserts its return value, it is the fixture-only proof this task exists to replace — the unit specs already passed for the whole time production had zero callers. It must render the app and read what production computed.
2. Did BOTH drills redden a LIVE integration test by name? Record which test and which assertion for each. A drill that reddened only a performance/ unit test does not satisfy DoD 6.
3. `grep -rln 'effort\|Effort' apps/control-room/src/live/` must now return the edge, the call site and the test — the measurement that was empty in step 1 is the proof the gap closed.
4. Was anything the children landed re-implemented? Re-declaring a code, layer, decision kind or interval kind that effort-records.ts already freezes is a silent duplicate.
5. Did dispatch behaviour change? A command that dispatched before must dispatch identically now, and a recording failure must never fail a dispatch.
6. Was `packages/store` touched, or `packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts` hand-edited? Both are forbidden; the generated client is codegen from @moe/contracts marked DO NOT EDIT BY HAND, and needing a new wire field means reporting blocked and naming a contracts codegen task.
7. Any stray `.js` bridge created under apps/control-room? That convention does not exist here.
8. Any probe, scratch or generated evidence file left behind? Epic rail 5.

COMMIT BY EXPLICIT PATHSPEC naming only the owned paths. Never `git add -A` (epic rail 3). If a foreign whole-tree commit already swept your bytes in, do NOT amend, reset or re-commit to claim it — hand QA the base-ref diff over the owned paths.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING. Timing got its live edge — live-event-feed.ts imports wire-timing.js, live-app.tsx mounts it through main.tsx, and live-timing-path.test.tsx guards the rendered result. Weakening effort-admission.ts's guard right now would redden a unit test in performance/, not a live integration test, because no live integration test for effort exists. A hardening slice whose drill can only redden a unit test has not hardened the integration — so this plan LANDS THE MISSING EDGE and the live test that the drill reddens.
